family: PhRMA DTC Guiding Principles & PhRMA Code

source.document: PhRMA Guiding Principles: Direct to Consumer Advertisements About Prescription Medicines (revised Oct 2018, effective Apr 15 2019)

rules.rule_text: DTC information should be accurate, truthful, not misleading, evidence-supported, balanced, consistent with labeling; no off-label promotion.
rules.verbatim_quote: companies should continue to base promotional claims on FDA approved labeling and not promote medicines for off-label uses

detection.question: Is every DTC claim consistent with labeling and free of off-label suggestion?
detection.fail_anchor: Any off-label suggestion or unsupported claim.

source.document: PhRMA Guiding Principles: Direct to Consumer Advertisements About Prescription Medicines (revised Oct 2018, effective Apr 15 2019)

rules.rule_text: DTC TV and print ads should clearly indicate the medicine is a prescription drug.
rules.verbatim_quote: should clearly indicate that the medicine is a prescription drug

detection.logic: DTC TV/print: require prescription|Rx[- ]only|ask your doctor (if|about) <brand>.

source.document: PhRMA Guiding Principles: Direct to Consumer Advertisements About Prescription Medicines (revised Oct 2018, effective Apr 15 2019)

rules.rule_text: DTC print ads should include FDA's MedWatch number and website; DTC TV should direct to a print ad with MedWatch and/or a company toll-free number.
rules.verbatim_quote: DTC print advertisements for prescription medicines should include FDA's toll-free MedWatch telephone number and website

detection.logic: Print: 1-800-FDA-1088 and fda.gov/medwatch. TV: MedWatch, print-ad reference, or a toll-free number.

source.document: PhRMA Guiding Principles: Direct to Consumer Advertisements About Prescription Medicines (revised Oct 2018, effective Apr 15 2019)

rules.rule_text: If actors portray health care professionals, the ad should say so; real HCPs who are compensated should be identified as such.
rules.verbatim_quote: should acknowledge in the advertisement that actors are being used

detection.logic: If meta.actor_portrays_hcp: require 'actor portrayal|actor'; if meta.real_hcp_compensated: require 'paid|compensated' disclosure.

source.document: PhRMA Guiding Principles: Direct to Consumer Advertisements About Prescription Medicines (revised Oct 2018, effective Apr 15 2019)

rules.rule_text: Celebrity endorsements should reflect the endorser's actual opinions/experience; company keeps verification, incl. whether the endorser uses the product.
rules.verbatim_quote: Companies should maintain verification of the basis of any actual or implied endorsements made by the celebrity endorser

detection.logic: Same as C-END-01 (verification record required for celebrity use claims).

source.document: PhRMA Guiding Principles: Direct to Consumer Advertisements About Prescription Medicines (revised Oct 2018, effective Apr 15 2019)

rules.rule_text: DTC TV that names a product should clearly state the approved conditions and the major risks.
rules.verbatim_quote: should clearly state the health conditions for which the medicine is approved and the major risks

detection.logic: TV pieces naming the brand: require indication statement (pi.indication_terms) and risk content.

source.document: PhRMA Guiding Principles: Direct to Consumer Advertisements About Prescription Medicines (revised Oct 2018, effective Apr 15 2019)

rules.rule_text: Balanced presentation: risks (incl. substance of boxed warnings) with reasonably comparable prominence, clear, conspicuous, neutral, without distraction.
rules.verbatim_quote: risks and safety information, including the substance of relevant boxed warnings, should be presented with reasonably comparable prominence to the benefit information

detection.question: Are risks (incl. boxed-warning substance) presented with reasonably comparable prominence, clearly and without distraction?
detection.pass_anchor: Comparable prominence; boxed-warning substance stated; no distraction.
detection.fail_anchor: Risk de-emphasized or distracted; boxed warning substance missing.

source.document: PhRMA Guiding Principles: Direct to Consumer Advertisements About Prescription Medicines (revised Oct 2018, effective Apr 15 2019)

rules.rule_text: DTC advertising should respect the seriousness of the condition and the medicine.
rules.verbatim_quote: All DTC advertising should respect the seriousness of the health conditions and the medicine being advertised

detection.question: Does the tone respect the seriousness of the condition and medicine (no trivializing humor, 'hype' framing of risks, lifestyle-only framing)?

source.document: PhRMA Guiding Principles: Direct to Consumer Advertisements About Prescription Medicines (revised Oct 2018, effective Apr 15 2019)

rules.rule_text: DTC ads with content inappropriate for children should run where the audience is ~90% adults.
rules.verbatim_quote: reasonably expected to draw an audience of approximately 90 percent adults (18 years or older)

source.document: PhRMA Guiding Principles: Direct to Consumer Advertisements About Prescription Medicines (revised Oct 2018, effective Apr 15 2019)

rules.rule_text: DTC TV naming a product should direct patients to cost information (list price, typical out-of-pocket).
rules.verbatim_quote: should include direction as to where patients can find information about the cost of the medicine

detection.logic: DTC TV: require cost|price|out-of-pocket|savings|afford within text/SUPERs, ideally with URL.

source.document: PhRMA Code on Interactions with Health Care Professionals (2022 revision)
source.section: Section 7 (Speaker Programs and Speaker Training Meetings)

rules.rule_text: Speaker programs: substantive education; only attendees with bona fide educational need; modest meals; no alcohol; appropriate venue with rep present; no repeat attendance; FMV compensation; sponsor clearly identified.
rules.verbatim_quote: Companies should not pay for or provide alcohol in connection with the speaker program.

detection.logic: Same metadata check as D-SP-*; plus deck text must identify sponsor ('sponsored by|on behalf of <company>').

source.document: PhRMA Code on Interactions with Health Care Professionals (2022 revision)

rules.rule_text: Rep informational presentations may include occasional modest meals in office/hospital settings; no entertainment (Section 3).

detection.logic: meta.program.type=='rep_presentation': venue must be in-office/hospital; meal modest; no entertainment.
